notes: Wealth manager CIO post series with extracted winning positions and no portfolio total, an undisclosed CPA endorsement, a never-sell guarantee and an unexplained historical simulation of the spending reserve, with a balanced rebalancing post as the decoy.

planted.span: Our three best ideas of 2025 were a mid-cap semiconductor equipment maker (up 94%), a regional railcar lessor (up 61%) and a specialty property insurer (up 47%).
planted.explanation: Three winning positions are shown with their individual returns, and no performance of the stock sleeve or client portfolios they were selected from is shown or offered.

planted.span: "When one of my clients is two or three years from retirement, Fairlop Wendt is the first call I make," says Janelle Strome, CPA, managing partner of Castlerow Tax & Accounting in Meridian.
planted.explanation: The CPA's endorsement carries no disclosure that she is not a client, whether she receives referral or other compensation, or the conflict created by the referral relationship the post describes.

planted.span: With three years of spending set aside, a market decline will never force a Fairlop Wendt client to sell stocks at a loss to pay their bills.
planted.explanation: The absolute claim cannot be substantiated, because a decline lasting longer than three years or withdrawals above plan would exhaust the reserve and require sales.

planted.span: Even so, when we ran our reserve rules through every rolling 25-year retirement since 1928, a client with a three-year reserve finished with more money than one without it in 64 of those 74 periods.
planted.explanation: The result of applying the firm's reserve rules to past periods no client actually experienced is hypothetical performance, shown with no description of the withdrawal rate, asset mix, fees or other assumptions used and no statement of its risks and limitations.

decoys.span: The benefit is that we trade when the mix has actually moved, which can mean fewer trades in quiet years and a portfolio that stays closer to the risk level you signed up for.
decoys.why_ok: The benefit is immediately followed by the costs and limitations of threshold rebalancing (more trades and taxable gains in volatile years, selling winners, lagging an unrebalanced portfolio in a long rally).
